Subject: Post-demo: 1M-token TCO probe & proposed test plan

Hi Sophie — thanks again for your time today. Quick recap and a concrete next-steps proposal so we can validate the economics you care about (per-1M tokens, batching impact, and cache hit behavior).

Recap (what we showed)
- Redwood hosted API: streaming + structured output with prefix KV cache (demo used a customer-like 1k prompt prefix).
- Live comparison against CloudScale managed endpoint (same model family we agreed on) — we showed a ~28% token-cost delta given 8x batching and aggressive KV reuse.
- Observability: per-request token breakdown and P95 latency traces in Console.

Immediate questions we want to answer for Novacorp
1) Realistic per-1M token unit cost for your traffic mix (short prompts vs long chat sessions).
2) Latency tail under your concurrency profile (P50/P95/P99).
3) Effective unit-econ with prefix cache hit rates (you mentioned heavy prefix reuse for SOPs).

Proposed test plan (short, measurable)
A. Synthetic 1M-token cost simulation: run three workload profiles ("support chat" — median prompt 60 tokens, "assistant longform" — median 1,200 tokens, "batch translate" — batched requests) and report effective $/1M tokens for Redwood hosted, Redwood Dedicated (reserved gpu), and CloudScale managed.
B. Batching sensitivity: measure cost and P95 at batch sizes 1, 4, 8; include per-request latency distribution and GPU utilization.
C. Cache hit matrix: run identical sessions with KV cache hit rates of ~30%, 60%, 90% to show marginal token saving and latency delta.
D. A/B endpoint test (if you want): route 10% traffic to Redwood hosted vs CloudScale for 48 hours to capture real-traffic numbers.

Deliverables and timing
- I can run A–C in our sandbox environment and share the workbook (+ recording) in 3 business days once you confirm test profiles.
- If you opt for D, we’ll need an API key and ~2 hours of engineering set-up on both sides; results in 2–3 business days after start.

Attachments: I’ve attached a starter TCO workbook (novacorp_1M_token_tco_table.xlsx) and the demo recording.

Ask: Can you confirm the three workload profiles above match your expectations? Also, do you want us to include CloudScale’s higher-availability multi-az pricing in the comparison or keep it to single-region managed endpoints?

Thanks — Mateo
Mateo Alvarez
Enterprise Solutions, Redwood Inference

Thanks Mateo — that outline looks right. A couple clarifying items before we lock the profiles:

- For support chat, median 60 tokens is accurate; top-heavy tail up to 500 tokens.
- For longform assistant the 1,200 median is fine. We do see some 2k+ conversations but they’re rare.
- For batch translate, we typically batch 8 at a time in our pipeline.

Two asks:
1) Can you surface normalized $/1M tokens that include any request-level fixed costs (e.g., per-request routing or bundling) so procurement can compare apples-to-apples?
2) Security question: does Redwood persist KV cache entries on disk or in ephemeral GPU memory? We need to know retention/default purge policy for compliance (SOC 2 scope).

If the answers look good, we’re happy to proceed with the A–C runs. I’m available Tue/Wed next week for a 30-minute sync to review the workbook.

— Sophie
Sophie Lam
Director, Platform Engineering — Novacorp

Hi Sophie — quick answers inline and then proposed dates.

- Normalized $/1M tokens: yes — we’ll include request-level fixed costs (route, API overhead) and show both gross token cost and all-in unit cost (tokens + per-request amortized). Workbook will have consolidated cells for procurement.
- KV cache persistence: default behavior in hosted is encrypted in-memory (ephemeral, persisted to managed KV only for short-term failover; retention default 24h with configurable TTL). For Private/Dedicated installs we offer customer-managed KMS and options to disable any disk-backed cache. I’ll attach a short note from Security with SOC 2 scope references.

Proposed calendar: Tue 2027-04-29 10:00–10:30 PT or Wed 2027-04-30 09:00–09:30 PT to walk the workbook — which works for you?

Planned test owners and rough ETA
- A–C runs: Redwood SRE (me) + Ben (bench configs) — results in 3 business days after confirm.
- If Novacorp opts for A/B, we’ll need an API key and a small routing rule; that adds 2 days for setup and 48 hours of run-time.

Notes on comparators: we’ll run CloudScale managed (single-region), plus a synthetic self-host reference (on equivalent GPU fleet) to show delta if you were to self-manage. That should make the trade-offs explicit.

I’ll drop the workbook and a short security note in this thread by EOD.

Best — Mateo
